issues.reason: 'Regularly' is a frequency adverb (a quantifier over occasions), and Manner is defined for the adverb answering 'how', so the instruction set's own remedy for a frequency adverbial that fits neither the strength+QuantifierPhrase channel nor Every/TimesPer applies verbatim: 'leave the unrepresentable adverbial out rather than mis-slot it'.

The genitive rule's single test ('is the possessed a part / component of the possessor?') licenses PartOf here, and the instruction set itself assigns PartOf both jobs — component-of-an-object and member-of-a-group — so the collision the reviewer describes is a property of the licensed vocabulary, not content the parser got wrong.

gaps_confirmed: a frequency adverb on an IMPERATIVE: the strength channel and the QuantifierPhrase companion both need a generic/habitual subject-and-predicate that a sealed Directive does not provide, and Every / TimesPer need a stated period or rate
new_gaps: a possessive of-phrase whose possessor is a definite PLURAL ('the exterior of the cabinets'): the genitive rule is stated for a single possessor, and nothing says whether the part attaches to the group symbol or distributes to each member
repair_summary: Dropped (Manner sk_clean_1 regularly) and (Manner sk_maintain_1 regularly) from inside the two Directive seals, leaving the adverbial unencoded per the leave-it-out instruction; nothing else changed.
notes: The rest of the imperative routing is correct — coordinated VPs translated independently, no addressee minted, the definite object's typing projected outside the seal, and no tense or occurrence asserted.
